custom.context:
Settlement:
During a typical settlement, solicitors adjust the sale price so the rates for the current period are shared between vendor and purchaser in proportion to their respective periods of ownership. Neither party needs to contact council the transfer of name on the property is handled automatically by the Titles Office.
What is a Supplementary Notice?:
An additional rates notice issued between the regular six-monthly notices, usually because something has changed about how the property is rated. Most often triggered by a property sale or subdivision involving bulk-assessed land but can also be triggered by revaluation without a sale.
Bulk Assessed Properties:
In rural zones it is common for a single Property ID to cover multiple lots. In {{var_sys_mapping}}, the selected lot boundary shows in red and related bulk-assessed lots show in orange these share a PID and appear on the same rates notice.
When land is bulk assessed, the State Government (Department of Resources) values the lots collectively as a single large parcel, resulting in a lower per-hectare valuation and lower rates. When individual lots within a bulk-assessed property are sold or subdivided off, each gets its own PID and is revalued independently by the State typically at a higher per-lot value, resulting in a higher rates charge.
Council has no discretion over State-set valuations. Customers who dispute a valuation have 60 days from the date of the valuation notice to lodge a formal objection with the Department of Resources.
Why is a supplementary notice's bill larger than expected?:
A standard rates notice covers a six-month period. A supplementary notice may cover a longer period sometimes a full year or more depending on when the change took effect. Always check the dates the notice covers before comparing it to a regular notice.
Because settlement contracts generally do not allow time for revaluation and a supplementary rates notice to be issued before the settlement period ends, the standard practice is for the vendor to ensure all rates owing on the property are paid in full prior to settlement.

Customer-facing script Building vs Planning Approval:
Building Approval Not Required?:
Some structures may not require building approval under Schedule 2 of the Building Regulation 2021 (Qld). Common examples include structures under 3m high that are not fences, retaining walls, or swimming pools; sun hoods under 2m2; tents under 100m2; and certain rural agricultural structures set back 200m from roads and boundaries.
Do not confirm over the phone that building approval is not required project-specific details matter and advice given without full context could be incorrect. Provide general information, refer the customer to the Schedule 2 link below, and offer to arrange a callback with the building team if they feel it is necessary.
Tiny homes, prefab & shipping containers:
These get asked about constantly and the most common misconception is that "tiny" or "prefab" means the normal rules don't apply. They do. See the context panel for how to explain this to the customer.

steps.title: Check the zone on Intramaps BEFORE answering Rural, Rural Re
steps.sop: Check the zone on {{var_sys_mapping}} BEFORE answering Rural, Rural Residential, Residential, or Township. Rural and urban zones have different setback rules.
steps.script: Planning approval asks: can this use happen on this land? It's about where the building goes and how it's sited. Building approval asks: is the structure itself safe and compliant? It's about how the building is constructed. Many houses only need building approval if your site ticks every box on the Rural Zone Checklist (or falls inside the Planning Scheme's acceptable outcomes for residential), no planning approval is required.

The most common call in Building is "do I need approval for this small project?" Use the rules of thumb below, then confirm specifics with the building team or the customer's certifier.
Rules of thumb:
- Extensions: always need building approval. Into a setback also planning approval or siting concession.
- Decks/patios attached to dwelling: building approval. Over 1m above natural ground level balustrades compliant with Building Code.
- Sheds over 10m2: building approval. Under 10m2 self-assessable but must meet siting rules.
- Carports: building approval. Open carports may sit within front setback under QDC MP 1.2 A1(c) (supports/walls in setback 15% of perimeter).
- Retaining walls over 1m: building approval + engineering design + Form 15.
- Fences over 2m: building approval. Pool fencing has its own standard see Pool node.

custom.context:
Town planning manages how land is used to create functional, sustainable communities guiding growth, protecting the environment, and ensuring access to services.
Customer-facing script the 3 pathways:
Common confusion to defuse early: "Assessable" is NOT the same as "Prohibited". Most things that aren't automatically Accepted are Assessable meaning they CAN be approved, just not without going through a formal planning application. When a customer hears "the Scheme doesn't allow it as Accepted development," many assume that's a refusal. It's a pathway. Worth saying out loud.
Your role:
You will regularly speak to customers about planning matters. You can help by:
The Planning Scheme is shaped by THREE parties useful to know:
- Community feedback public consultation during scheme reviews
- State regulators must align with State Planning Policy and regional plans
- Council manages day-to-day, assesses applications, leads scheme reviews
That tri-party structure is why planning decisions sometimes feel more constrained than Council would prefer neither Council nor residents alone set the rules.
The Planning Scheme is changing. A new draft Southern Downs Planning Scheme is in development with consultation open at haveyoursay.sdrc.qld.gov.au. Decisions on current applications continue under the existing scheme until the new one is formally adopted.
Common customer questions:
Do I need planning approval? / Can I subdivide? / What is the difference between planning and building approval? / What is the status of my application?

custom.context:
Plenty of small businesses operate legitimately from home WITHOUT any planning approval online retailers, consultants, tutors, bookkeepers, tradies whose work happens at other sites, family day care, B&Bs. The Planning Scheme has a dedicated Home Based Business framework (section 9.3.4) that defines what fits within self-assessable limits.
Customer-facing script:
NO planning approval if ALL of these apply:
[ ] Size: 40m in Residential, 100m in Rural
[ ] Staff: only residents (Residential) or residents + 1 off-site employee (Rural)
[ ] Clients on site: max 6 at a time, 8am-7pm Mon-Sat (excl. public holidays)
[ ] Signage: 1 sign max, 0.3m, name/occupation/contact only
[ ] No retail sales from premises (online/mail order OK)
[ ] Vehicles: 1 commercial (2 in Rural), no vehicle >4.5t in Residential
[ ] NOT a motor vehicle workshop or medium/high-impact industry
Family Day Care specific rule:
Family day care fits inside the Home Based Business framework with one specific cap max 6 children under school age at any one time. Other limits above still apply.
B&B / Airbnb / short-term accommodation different pathway:
Customers asking about renting a room, doing Airbnb, or running a B&B should be routed to the Short-Term Accommodation workflow rather than Home Based Business. Even small operations need a separate building reclassification from Class 1a to Class 1b and a Local Law permit to Operate Rental Accommodation plus the rates category changes. The Home Based Business framework doesn't cover that approval stack.
If outside any limit MCU required:
Don't oversell as a refusal. Many step-outside-the-limits operations get approved with conditions on hours, parking, signage, neighbour notification.
Other permits potentially needed:
- Food Business Licence (Food Act 2006) for food preparation/sales separate from planning
- Personal Appearance Services licence (Public Health Act 2003) for body piercing, tattooing, beauty therapy required regardless of setting
Outside Council remit but worth mentioning:
ABN (ABR), tax (ATO), Working with Children check (Blue Card), liquor licence (OLGR), WorkCover. Business Queensland (business.qld.gov.au) has good checklists.

custom.context:
This catches a lot of operators by surprise. Even a small Airbnb-style let of an existing house requires more than just planning there's an approval stack of 3 (sometimes 4) separate approvals, and the rates category changes too.
Customer-facing script set expectations early:
The approval stack applies to ALL short-term accommodation:
TRIAGE first question to ask:
"Is the property in town (Low/Medium Density Residential) or rural?"
IN TOWN (Low or Medium Density Residential) Airbnb-style:
Most permissive path in the scheme. No planning approval needed IF all of:
[ ] Existing dwelling (not new build, not converted shed)
[ ] Max 6 guests at any one time
[ ] Meets acceptable outcomes (parking, amenity, signage, hours)
If can't meet every AO: code-assessable MCU.
If >6 guests / new building / non-dwelling building: impact-assessable MCU (public notification, Council meeting).
Still need building reclassification + Local Law permit even when no planning approval needed.
RURAL ZONE (cabins, farm-stay, motel-style):
Planning approval ALWAYS required. Two code-assessable brackets:
- Lot 5ha + 2 buildings + 12 guests code
- Lot 10ha + 4 buildings + 24 guests code
- Anything outside those brackets impact
CARAVAN PARK / CAMPING GROUND (Rural only):
Different defined use. Planning approval ALWAYS required.
- Lot 10ha + 20 sites code
- Larger or smaller lot impact
Also subject to Caravan Parks Local Law for ongoing operation (amenities ratios, dump points, waste management).
Building reclassification what's triggered:
Class 1b building requirements (designed for paying guests):
[ ] Interconnected hard-wired smoke alarms every bedroom + every corridor serving bedrooms
[ ] Evacuation lighting activated by smoke alarm
[ ] Balustrades to BCA standards on any deck/landing > 1m above ground
[ ] Disabled access to 1 bedroom + bathroom (if 4 guest bedrooms)
[ ] Bushfire overlay properties additional requirements per Bushfire Hazard Overlay factsheet
Lodgement building reclassification:
- Email sdrcbuilding@sdrc.qld.gov.au or attend Admin Centre in person
- Package: DA Form 2, site plan, floor plan (showing smoke alarms / escape lighting / exit doors), QBCC Insurance Certificate OR Owner Builder Permit
- Decision within 35 business days of complete information
- Final result: Form 11 Certificate of Occupancy issued (NOT Form 21 Form 21 is for a new Class 1a dwelling; Form 11 is for the reclassification)
Local Law permit:
Lodged AFTER the building reclassification is complete. See Licences & Permits for Business page on the SDRC website.
Other things worth knowing:
- Food licence if any food served (breakfast, mini-bar items prepared on-site) separate licence under Food Act 2006
- State environmental approvals may apply for larger rural sites without reticulated sewerage
- Infrastructure charges apply to most planning approvals

steps.title: Planning approval sometimes required (depends on zone, scale
steps.sop: Planning approval sometimes required (depends on zone, scale, guest numbers). Often NOT required for letting an existing house in town to 6 guests.

It's all manageable but it pays to understand the full picture before you commit money. Many owners get blindsided by the building reclassification because the house already exists and they assume nothing needs doing but the reclassification is required regardless of whether any physical work happens.

Customer-facing script important context:
Action - run through checklist with customer:
To be a properly made submission it must:
[ ] Be in writing and signed by each person making the submission
[ ] Be received during the public notification period
[ ] Include the name and address of all submitters
[ ] Include the grounds of the submission, and the facts and circumstances relied upon in support of those grounds
[ ] Include one (1) postal or electronic address for all submission-makers
[ ] Be addressed to the assessment manager: Southern Downs Regional Council
Grounds that CARRY WEIGHT (relate to Planning Scheme):
- Impact on traffic, noise, amenity
- Hours of operation, overshadowing
- Character of the area
- Stormwater, environmental values
Grounds that do NOT carry weight (personal/commercial):
- Disliking the applicant
- Competing with the proposed business
- Diminution of property value
Council assesses applications against the Planning Scheme not against commercial or personal interests.
If the application is APPROVED despite submissions:
Properly-made submitters have a right of appeal to the Planning & Environment Court (20 bd appeal window after applicant's).
If the application is REFUSED:
All submitters notified and receive a copy of the Decision Notice.
Council can't tell the customer WHAT to say in a submission that would be inappropriate but can clarify the process, timeframes, and what the scheme considers relevant. Refer to duty planner if unsure.

Breeding sits across state law (Queensland Dog Breeder Register, microchipping) and Council local laws (cat breeder permits, Planning Scheme for higher numbers). Important to be clear about who runs what.
TRIAGE first question to ask:
"Are you breeding dogs or cats?"
DOG BREEDING STATE LAW
Customer-facing script:
Key facts to know:
[ ] Cutoff date: applies to dogs born on or after 26 May 2017 only (not retrospective)
[ ] Must register within 28 days of a litter being born
[ ] Registration is free, valid 12 months, annual renewal
[ ] Applies to ALL breeders professional, occasional, \"mum and dad\", accidental
[ ] Supply number must be included in microchip info + displayed on every advertisement + provided to new owner
[ ] Pet shops/retailers must use the original breeder\'s supply number when on-selling
[ ] Penalties apply for sale or gifting without a supply number
Working Dog Exemption narrow:
Primary producers breeding working dogs on rural land for other primary producers to use as working dogs are EXEMPT. The legal definition of \"working dog\":
[ ] Kept on rural land
[ ] By a primary producer (or someone employed by one)
[ ] Primarily for droving, protecting, tending or working stock (or being trained for it)
Pig-dogs are explicitly NOT working dogs under the Act. The definition is limited to dogs working stock managing feral animals doesn\'t qualify.
If a primary producer supplies ANY puppy from a litter for a non-working purpose (sold to a non-primary-producer, kept as a pet, given to a friend in town), they MUST register as a breeder for that puppy.
Breeder Exemption Numbers special cases:
For one-off scenarios where someone is supplying a dog they didn\'t breed:
[ ] Found stray they want to rehome
[ ] Owner rehoming their own dog (not as a business)
[ ] Primary producer selling a working dog to a non-primary-producer
A separate Breeder Exemption Number is required for EACH individual dog. Apply through the same QDBR portal.
How to direct the customer:
Up to 4 breeding cats Council Animal Breeder Permit:
If customer wants to keep more cats than the standard limit (see Registration/Keeping branch for table), they can apply for an Animal Breeder Permit for up to 4 breeding cats.
Application requirements:
[ ] Completed application form
[ ] Plans and details of cats\' enclosure
[ ] Application fee (Fees & Charges)
[ ] Written evidence of affiliation with a recognised cat breeder association
[ ] Registration of all breeding cats with that association
More than 4 breeding cats Planning approval (Animal Keeping):
Triggers a planning application under the Planning Scheme:
[ ] Rural zone, lot at least 20 hectares, fewer than 10 cats Code assessable
[ ] All other situations Impact assessable (public notification required)
Route Planning enquiries to the duty planner on 1300 697 372.
Microchipping requirements apply regardless of breeder status every cat supplied must be microchipped before it leaves the breeder\'s care.

custom.context:
For locations and trading hours refer to the Waste Facility Flyer, or the context panel below for a quick reference.
For guidance on specific items, use Recycle Mate first an interactive map tool that lets users search by item type to find nearby facilities. Also includes a chatbot for detailed disposal advice.
Free at Council facilities:
Scrap metal, clean concrete and bricks, e-waste, empty agvet chemical containers (drumMUSTER), used motor oil at some sites, and clean timber pallets.
Fees apply to:
General household waste, mattresses, tyres, whitegoods, construction and demolition waste. Fees are set in the annual Fees & Charges schedule.
Green waste:
Grass clippings, prunings, and small branches can go in the red/green lid general waste bin. Do NOT put green waste in the yellow recycling bin. Larger loads can go to a Council waste facility FREE for residents, commercial green waste attracts a disposal fee. Composting at home is a great option Council has Worm Farming and Composting fact sheets.
Trickle tape (T-tape):
Council stockpiles clean trickle tape for recycling at the Stanthorpe Waste Management Facility, FREE of charge. The tape must be separated from plastic mulch and as free as possible from soil, roots, and organic matter. Contaminated tape cannot be recycled and attracts landfill fees for commercial operators. Site supervisors direct the customer to the stockpile on arrival.
Specific items:
[ ] Asbestos: customer must pre-book and complete the Asbestos Disposal Form before attending. Page 1 is for Commercial, Page 2 for Domestic. Must be double-bagged in 200-micron plastic and clearly labelled.
[ ] Deceased pets: small pets (birds, fish, guinea pigs) can go in the general waste bin. Larger pets should be taken to the closest accepting waste facility. Burial is only available at the Warwick Waste Management Facility. Prior notice required for bulk loads.
[ ] Ammunition, explosives, old fireworks: NEVER in any bin or waste facility. Refer customer to the Queensland Explosives Inspectorate on 1300 739 868 (24-hour hotline).
[ ] Solar Panels: storm-damaged solar panels are being accepted until 1 July 2026 at Pratten, Warwick, and Stanthorpe. Otherwise refer to CDS Recycling for e-waste recycling.
[ ] Batteries: never in a kerbside bin. Take to any supervised Council waste facility (Ecobatt partnership). Tape terminals on lithium batteries.
Please don't let customers dump green waste on bushland, verges, or waterways spreads pest plants, fuels bushfires, attracts wildlife to roadsides. See Illegal Dumping node.
For anything not covered, contact the waste team.

custom.context:
Council CAN investigate "unlawful land use" under the Planning Scheme.
Customer-facing script:
Triage is this likely a permitted Home Based Business?:
The Planning Scheme has a defined Home Based Business framework. An operation that fits inside ALL of these limits is generally permitted without approval:
[ ] Area used for business up to 40m in residential zones, up to 100m in rural
[ ] Staff only residents (or +1 non-resident employee in rural)
[ ] Clients on site max 6 at any one time, 8am-7pm Mon-Sat only
[ ] Signage one sign, max 0.3m, occupier name and contact only
[ ] No retail sales from the premises (mail order / online sales are fine)
[ ] No outside storage
[ ] One commercial vehicle (two in Rural), nothing over 4.5t in residential
[ ] Not a motor vehicle workshop, medium- or high-impact industry
If the complaint clearly describes activity OUTSIDE these limits (e.g. workshop with multiple employees, customer parking, large signage, commercial truck deliveries), lodge with confidence. If it's borderline, lodge anyway Planning Compliance will assess.
Common triggers that cross the line:
[ ] Commercial vehicle traffic
[ ] Employees arriving and leaving
[ ] Customer parking
[ ] Commercial signage
[ ] Industrial noise
[ ] Activities that change the character of the property
Short-term accommodation / Airbnb complaints different pathway. If the complaint is about a property being used for short-term guest accommodation (not a workshop or trade), route through Planning Compliance but flag "suspected unauthorised short-term accommodation" the assessment involves Building reclassification and Local Law permit status, not just the Home Based Business framework. See PlanSTA for the approval stack that should be in place.
Staff action:
Lodge {{var_sys_requests}} (Keyword: Planning Compliance) or online service request. Planning Compliance team investigates.

Feral pigs are a restricted invasive animal must not be kept, fed, or moved. Signs of pig activity: rooting damage, wallows near water, damaged fences, missing lambs or poultry.
Control options for landholders:
- Trapping with a pig-specific trigger silo-style cage with funnel entrance or lift-bar trigger. Pre-feed for several nights before setting the trigger to dramatically improve catch rates

- Ground and aerial shooting effective in low-density or open country, thermal imaging helps at night

- Deposit claimable within 3 months of return

Feral pigs can carry diseases transmissible to humans leptospirosis, brucellosis, Q fever, melioidosis. Wear gloves, avoid direct contact with blood/urine/faeces, don't eat undercooked feral pig meat, and never feed raw feral pig meat or offal to dogs (swine brucellosis can pass from pigs to dogs to humans).

custom.context:
The Southern Downs is home to the largest wild fallow deer herd in Queensland, centred on the Pikedale area south-west of Warwick. Broadly continuous with the NSW New England Tableland population.
Species locally:
Fallow deer (Dama dama) is the local species. Red, chital, and rusa deer are well north and east of SDRC.
Legal status:
Feral fallow deer are a category 3, 4 and 6 restricted invasive animal under the Biosecurity Act 2014 must not be moved, fed, given away, sold, or released. GBO applies.
Farmed deer / game parks:
Kept in deer-proof enclosures, treated separately. If an enclosed deer escapes and establishes in the wild, the owner is responsible. Anyone keeping deer must register as a biosecurity entity.
Control options for landholders:
- Ground shooting most effective and humane method; usually at night from a vehicle with spotlights or thermal equipment, by trained personnel with appropriate licences
- Helicopter shooting cost-effective across large or open properties but specialised; best coordinated across adjoining landholders
- Trapping option in peri-urban areas; self-closing gate or clover trap; must be checked frequently, animal welfare considerations significant
- Exclusion fencing works but expensive (approx 2.1m high, 9m posts, netting pegged to ground); usually only for high-value crops
- Engaging licensed recreational hunters common local approach; landholder should check access conditions, public liability insurance, and references first
Coordination matters:
Deer have large home ranges and move between properties. Control on a single property is usually eroded by in-migration coordinated effort across adjoining landholders is much more effective than working alone.
Staff action:
For property-specific advice, transfer to Local Laws or arrange callback ({{var_sys_requests}}: Deer).

Customer-facing script what actually reduces numbers:
steps.script: The four most effective things are: block access to nest sites in your roof and eaves (cover gaps, clear dead palm fronds, bird-proof gutters), don't feed them even accidentally (bring pet food inside, seal compost, watch your bird feeders), remove nests and eggs (Indian myna eggs are a distinctive blue-turquoise no native hollow-nester lays eggs that colour), and restore native habitat. Trapping is possible but needs coordination with neighbours to actually make a dent.
